title: Make the PR + green-CI close-out rule a run precondition, not model diligence
description:
Routed upstream from the ticks pwp run, 2026-09-15 (close-out tick 8vl, attempt 12).

The ticks repo states the rule in .tick/config.md Rules, verbatim:

  'Epic integration goes through a PR + CI gate: the orchestrator pushes the epic branch and opens a PR; the epic close-out may not complete until the CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) is green on that PR. No direct merges of epic branches to the default branch.'

ticfac pushes the epic branch and never opens the PR. The checkpoint carries no PR state and no CI state, so nothing in the run can tell whether the rule is met. Close-out attempts 11 and 12 each had to rediscover the same unmet precondition by reading the repo's config themselves, and each answered failed for it. The rule is enforced by whether the worker happens to read config.md and reason correctly — which is exactly the 'an orchestrator should remember it from a prompt' failure this project keeps rejecting.

Compounding it for this repo specifically: ci.yml triggers on pull_request and on push to main ONLY. A push to epic/pwp runs nothing. So without a PR there is not merely no green CI — there is no CI at all, and close-out's precondition is unsatisfiable rather than merely unmet.

Wanted:
- Read the rule from the target repo's config rather than hardcoding it, the way the gate reads runners.toml.
- Where the rule applies, treat 'a PR exists for the epic branch' and 'CI is green on it' as an ADMISSION PRECONDITION of the close-out phase: open the PR if absent, then hold close-out until CI is green or report a typed refusal naming the failing job.
- Record both facts in the checkpoint so a resumed run does not rediscover them, and so the feed says which one is unmet.

Acceptance: a test with a target repo declaring the rule asserts close-out is not admitted while no PR exists, that the run opens one, and that a red CI produces a typed refusal naming the job rather than a generic failure.
